title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ས (Derge Tengyur, vol. 107)
shelf_note: A Madhyamaka verse treatise on non-perception (anupalabdhi), direct perception and yogic gnosis as non-seeing. It belongs in the dbu ma section of the Derge Tengyur.
structure_note: The facsimile page number printed in the margin is '516' and the record is page 515. That looks like a constant scan-index offset, not a wrong leaf: the OCR matches this image.

ocr_errors.image: the image line-end reads more like 'འཇིག་རྟེན་ ... འདས་པ ... ཡི' with no doubled 'འདས་པ'; the OCR's eight syllables break the seven-syllable meter
ocr_errors.problem: probable dittography of འདས་པ in a verse line (the image is hard to read at the line end)
a variant-brace notation is left in the transcription text

tr_errors_A.english: That alone is the ultimate truth. Whatever seeing there is, is a non-seeing.
tr_errors_A.problem: Misparsed. The verse says that the seeing OF the ultimate is a non-seeing. A turns it into two claims, 'that alone is ultimate truth' and a universal 'whatever seeing there is, is non-seeing'.

tr_errors_A.english: even if your own perception were mistaken, because it is uncertain, it is not established that the perceptions of everyone else are mistaken
tr_errors_A.problem: དམིགས་པ་ལོག་པ means non-apprehension (cessation of perception), not 'mistaken perception'. The argument is that one's own non-perception is inconclusive. The overall shape of the argument survives.

tr_errors_A.english: Since the nature of all phenomena is not established as being the pervaded or any such thing, how can it be certain that they are associated with anything?
tr_errors_A.problem: ཅི་སྟེ ('if') is read as 'how', and a negation ('is not established') is added that is not in the source. The conditional that leads into 'then it would be with entity' is lost.
the tail of a sentence from the previous folio is presented as a standalone claim

tr_errors_B.english: even if one's own perception were mistaken, because that is not universally certain, it is not established that everyone's perception is mistaken
tr_errors_B.problem: the same misreading of དམིགས་པ་ལོག་པ (non-apprehension) as 'mistaken perception'

tr_errors_B.english: How could the intrinsic nature of all phenomena be established as the pervaded and so forth in certain relation to anything?
tr_errors_B.problem: ཅི་སྟེ ('if') is rendered as a rhetorical 'how could', so the conditional is weakened

tr_errors_B.english: it is described by the non-deluded: there is no turning away from the genuine truth
tr_errors_B.problem: the next verse is joined to this one as reported speech, which the syntax does not clearly support

pages.prefer_reason: Both share the non-apprehension misreading, but A also misparses the key line on the seeing of the ultimate as non-seeing, and it adds a negation in the pervader argument.

book_verdict: The page is a sound Madhyamaka folio with a good OCR (minor markup residue and one probable doubled word). Both translations are usable. B is more faithful on the central claim that seeing the ultimate is non-seeing.
